messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated streaming tail latency observed in prod-rt (p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.1s) starting ~10:00 UTC. Affected path: /v1/streaming/generate (SSE). Error rates stable. Paging SRE oncall. Runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/streaming-tail
maya: reading apm traces now — I see a sharp rise in time-to-first-chunk for a subset of requests. traces point to proxy write queuing on edge-proxy-12.
jon: confirming, seeing backlog on edge-proxy-12 with many sockets in FIN_WAIT/WRITE backlog. Client retransmits increasing. Could be slow consumer or proxy-side write buffer saturation.
sasha: any deploys in the last hour? I don't see any in releases feed. No config rollouts.
lee: I'm on proxy calibration. Dumping netstat / lsof on edge-proxy-12 now.
lee: ```
# netstat -tanp | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
2400
# ss -s | grep -A2 "TCP:" 
TCP: inuse 2600 orphan 0 tw 1200
``` 
maya: 2400 concurrent established sockets is higher than normal for that host. We recently pushed a keepalive change but that was only to cf-proxy-09, not edge-proxy-12.
opsbot: Auto-scaling: edge-proxy pool at 80% CPU; cannot auto-add more due to AZ quota cap. (policy: burst via fallback region).
jon: I can repro with curl + chunked SSE client — if the client is slow to read, the proxy accumulates and then stalls delivery of subsequent chunks. We may be hitting send buffer limits and kernel backpressure.
sasha: Customer impact — quick check: top clients by failure/latency show two big integrators with 35% of streaming sessions hitting p99. Interactive apps may see delayed first tokens.
maya: Runbook step: enable write coalescing tuning and temporarily increase socket send buffer on proxies. Applying sysctl on edge-proxy-12 to net.core.wmem_max and net.ipv4.tcp_wmem.
lee: Applying now: ```
sudo sysctl -w net.core.wmem_max=16777216
sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_wmem="4096 16384 16777216"
``` 
lee: Also toggled proxy-level config: disable per-connection aggressive buffering for SSE (proxy.conf: stream_buffering=false) and reloaded.
jon: I pushed a canary update to 1 of 3 proxies in the pool. Monitoring to see if chunk delivery resumes normal cadence.
maya: Observability note: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 180ms on canary. p99 still at ~800ms for affected clients.
sasha: We should also look at client-side slow consumers. Any indication of large read pauses? tcpdump sampling shows many zero-window from client IP ranges for the integrators.
lee: Captured sample: ```
06:12:01.123 IP 10.10.2.1.52000 > edge-proxy-12.443: Flags [.], ack 12345, win 0
06:12:01.223 IP 10.10.2.1.52000 > edge-proxy-12.443: Flags [.], ack 12346, win 0
``` 
jon: Zero-window indicates client cannot read quickly — they might be overloaded. But we still need graceful behavior server-side: we shouldn't backlog so that unrelated sessions are impacted.
maya: Mitigation plan: 1) rollout proxy config change (stream_buffering false) to remaining proxies, 2) enable connection-level max-buffer-per-client to bound per-socket memory, 3) contact top integrator support to ask them to check consumer read loop.
sasha: I'm drafting a brief customer message. For now mark severity P2 since API responses still complete but with high tail latencies for some.
opsbot: Scaling update: quota request approved for extra proxy instances in fallback region; spinning up 4 new edge-proxy instances.
lee: Rolling the config to remaining proxies now (batch=2). Will keep one as control.
jon: After batch 1 (2 hosts) applied: p95 -> 160ms, p99 -> 420ms. Good improvement.
maya: Can we set an emergency route to route heavy integrator traffic to dedicated pivots with per-client limits? That would reduce cross-customer impact.
lee: We can add trafficclass routing by header cf-integrator-id and send to dedicated pool. Implementing rule now (rate-limited rollout).
sasha: Customer comms drafted: "We're seeing intermittent delays delivering streaming tokens for customers using long-lived connections. We're mitigating by bounding per-connection buffers and rolling proxy tuning; no data loss. ETA for full mitigation: 30-45m." Thoughts?
maya: Good. Add note to mention we've scaled proxies and engaged the integrator. Also link to status page entry.
jon: Postmortem notes to collect: timeline, kernel tunables, proxy buffering default gotcha, client zero-window occurrences, and potential long-term fix: per-tenant circuit breakers + backpressure shedding.
sasha: I'll own the customer follow-up and postmortem doc. Maya can lead technical remediation and ops playbook update.
maya: Oncall rotation: I'm handing to Jon for the next 30m while I join a customer call. Jon please escalate to platform if p99 > 1s persists after full rollout.
jon: Ack. I'll watch p99 and the control host. If we see regressions I'll revert the last change and reopen.
lee: All proxies rolled. p95 = 150ms, p99 = 250ms across the fleet. Client zero-window count down from ~1200 to ~150 in last 15m.
maya: Great work all. Leaving notes in incident channel and creating status page update.
opsbot: Incident update recorded: incident_id=INC-2026-2899, priority=P2, assigned=[maya, jon, sasha, lee], mitigation=buffer-bounds+proxy-tuning+scale
sasha: Thanks team. Will keep this thread open for postmortem edits and close after RCA completed.
jon: quick ops tip: add healthcheck to detect heavy zero-window bursts and alert before it hits tail latency SLOs.
maya: Agreed. Also add a test to chaos-suite for slow-read consumer scenarios so we catch this in staging.
incidents-bot: Incident marked as under control. Follow-up: RCA doc scheduled. :white_check_mark:
